name: Atlas Compendium · mission and system tables
source: Tables 1–42 extracted from the user-supplied Atlas Compendium chapters. Chapter prose is not included.

rows.d: Undercover infiltration of a base, smaller group or outpost to obtain data, identify leaders or investi- gate the organization.
Gather information from tags, library databases, networks, old scrolls or a living person.
Classic espionage with secret meetings, shadowing, burglaries and undercover work.
Kidnap someone and deliver the person to the employer.
Make sure sensitive information, resources or goods are delivered safely from the employer to the receiver.
Make sure a resource (information, person, object, ship) is safe from an attack or for a specified amount of time.
Trick a person or organization into believing false information, or make them perform a certain action, or set a chain of events in motion.
Acquire an artifact, usually from an unknown, underground location.
Rescue a resource (usually a person or group) that is held captive or hostage. It could also be an object or a wrecked spaceship.
Observe a resource (usually a person) for a specified amount of time.
Murder someone, sometimes so that it looks like an accident. Collateral damage is permitted.
A bunker, catacombs or caves.
Inhospitable planet side wilderness. Usually far from cities or settlements.
A bazaar or market in a city or settlement.
Spaceport on a space station or planet.
The surface of an asteroid or a smaller moon. Vacuum or dangerous atmosphere.
On a small space station, anything from an oxygen oasis to a trade or service station.
Firstcome or Portal Builder ruins.
A small colony, usually no bigger than a small, sparsely populated village. Far from other settlements.
A portal station next to a sun.
Onboard a spaceship during voyage or docking.

A small outpost, usually planet side. An outpost is commonly just a single building with a specific func- tion and only a few inhabitants. For example sensor station, dam control station, courier post or some other communications station.

Another patron or a person with a similar background as the employer is after the same thing. Could offer the group higher payment or that they will use the information/resource for a different purpose when the mission is completed.
The employer wants to come along for the mission, or send an observer or agent along.
A person the PCs encounter is a double agent for another organization with a conflicting agenda.
A piece of information about the mission turns out to be false, either intentionally or by mistake.
The group's opponent receive backup in the form of reinforcements, more advanced computer systems or some other form of extra assistance.
The employer wants the mission to go badly and for the PCs to take the fall for something.
An intelligence agency, possibly factionary, with many resources has the same or opposite goals as the PCs.
Scout out an area, a location or the surroundings of a building. Remain unnoticed and report back to the employer.
Attack and hold a location. Prisoners may be taken.
Defend a location or patrol an area; prevent the enemy from seizing it.
Support or reinforce a position under attack, repel the enemy.
Find a person, group or location and destroy it. Could be civilians, enemy combatants or vehicles/ spaceships.
Protect a resource. It could be information, a person, an object or a ship. Protect it from an attack or guard it for a specified amount of time.
Locate a person, group or object and either retrieve it or notify the employer of its location.
Rescue a group, squadron or spaceship from an attack, imprisonment, or some other peril.
Plan and execute a raid on a person, group, convoy or vehicle. The goal is usually to destroy or delay the target.
Locate something important, for example nuclear warheads, antimatter bombs or bionic weapons. The PCs could be accompanied by an agent, a weapons expert or some other officer.
Go behind enemy lines or breach a fortress or garrison to secure a resource that could be a person, information or an object.
A bunker, new or old.
Inhospitable planet side wilderness. Usually far from cities or settlements.
A trench on a deadlocked frontline. Mine fields, underground tunnels and other soldiers in despair.
Spaceport on a space station or planet.
The surface of an asteroid or a smaller moon. Vacuum or dangerous atmosphere.
A fortified space station with weapon systems, or some other battle installation such as a larger garri- son, hangars or docks.
A larger area where open war is raging. Could be a burned-out city or a wilderness full of fighting combatants.
A fortification could be a wall, modern fort, castle, artillery position, rocket silo or mine field.
On a small space station, anything from an oxygen oasis to a trade or service station.
Onboard a spaceship during voyage or docking.

A small outpost, usually planet side. An outpost is commonly just a single building with a specific func- tion and only a few inhabitants. For example sensor station, guard post, smaller garrison, smaller arsenal or warehouse.
A piece of information about the contract turns out to be false, either intentionally or by mistake.
Someone they must protect during the mission accompanies the group. It could be an observer, a civil- ian or an agent.
The group has gear problems. It could be anything from weapons to vehicles or spaceships.
The resistance or the attackers are stronger than expected.
The group's employer is captured during the mission. Fitting if the employer is an officer in the group's company.
A new offensive has just been initiated when the group is about to carry out their mission, either by the enemies or by the PCs' side in the conflict.
The area where the mission takes place is being bombed. It could be air raids, torpedo attacks or rebel forces detonating mines and homemade explosives.
Perform an excavation, start a dig site or help in an already started excavation.
Collect smaller archaeological finds, artifacts, information, scrolls or something similar. Could be from a dig site or some other location.
Map a location or an area for the employer. Report back with sensor maps and other collected data.
Protect a smaller colony such as a dig site, Bulletin station, sensor station or radio beacon from an attack or from nature's wrath for a specified amount of time.
Assist a smaller colony with gear, information or expert knowledge about exo use, medicurgy, con- struction or something else.
Find an artifact. The location and sometimes the function are unknown. Clues must be tracked down before departure.
Locate something important, for example lost ruins, a dig site or a surveyed location. The PCs could be accompanied by an external expert such as an archaeologist, correspondent or diplomat.
Find a specific piece of information for the employer. Sometimes, the group does not know the intended use of the information.
Command a prospecting expedition or secure a claim somewhere. It could be mining, asteroid harvest- ing, logging or gas or dust trawling.
Rescue a group, colony, archaeological expedition or correspondents from an attack or some other peril. Sometimes, the group does not know what has happened to the victims.
Command or join in an expedition hunting a monster or some other creature.
Catacombs, tombs or underground ruins.
Inhospitable planet side wilderness. Usually far from cities or settlements.
A library or database hub. Could contain anything from scrolls to memory tags and djinn memories.
The surface of a moon. Usually vacuum or dangerous atmosphere. Planet-like moons count as wilder- ness (above).
An asteroid belt or a debris or gas cloud.
Ruins, either Firstcome, unknown or created by a conflict.
Portal Builder remains. Usually mystical but sometimes intact or functioning.
A colony that lost contact with the Horizon several segments or cycles ago.
On a small space station, anything from an oxygen oasis to a trade or service station. Could be aban- doned or destroyed.
Onboard a spaceship during voyage or docking.

rows.n: One of the wonders of the Horizon
rows.d: A large size artifact, like artificial moons or micro suns. The GM is free to decide its exact nature.
A piece of information about the contract turns out to be false, either intentionally or by mistake.
The expedition is subjected to nature's wrath. It could be anything from ion storms, bad weather and meteorite showers to landslides or flash floods.
Corsairs attack the expedition.
A competing party has the same goal as the expedition and tries to get there first or stop the PCs. They have roughly the same gear as the PCs.
The destination is under blockade. It could be anything from tolls or anti-smuggling measures to fac- tionary war.
The destination is placed under quarantine. It could be because of a contagion, a mind meme, danger- ous technology or something else.
The expedition's goals interfere with the work of an intelligence agency. Intelligence agencies usually have a lot of resources and few scruples.
A pilgrimage to one of the Horizon's important temples or holy sites.
Bring supplies to somewhere.
Travel to a monastery and remain there for some time.
Establish a missionary colony and spread the faith in an area.
Travel to several locations and spread the faith.
Help build a temple, from construction to inauguration, perhaps staying on to run the temple.
Acquire a holy relic. It could be body part from a martyr or a hero, an object with sacred writing on it or a religious symbol.
Find a dangerous or tainted relic or a heathen idol and destroy it.
Find a lost prophet, seer, ascetic or preacher.
Help the Icons so that a prophecy is fulfilled.
Represent a temple in another location, such as during a sacred meeting, diplomatic trip or mis- sionary voyage.
Investigate and find lost literature. Could be anything from oral stories to blood operas or songs.
Service a set. Could be anything from make-up, lighting and camera operating to catering or relaxation.
Perform somewhere by special invitation.
Organize a carnival, coordinate with other entertainers, acrobats and circuses.
A series of smaller performances in a bazaar or market.
Work with a holo movie, acting and/or directing.
Perform a play in a theater or an opera house.
Perform in a circus show. Could be acrobatics, magic or animal/monster taming
Take part in a pleasure cruise for the rich.
Perform for high-ranking dignitaries or factionaries.
Put on a concert with musical instruments and/or singing.
Construct a new plantation and plant crops.
Bring supplies to somewhere.
Work in a factory or with service for a shorter period of time or one season. It could be harvesting, transportation, cleaning or servant work.
Build a colony or prepare a location before the colonists arrive.
Collect or tow an asteroid or ice block to prospectors or a refinery unit.
Build something big, such as a dam, a mine or a large complex like a spaceport or a station.
Exact vengeance on another group of plebeians or non-unionized workers. Could be sabotaging cargo or loading, burning stockpiled goods or destroying a ship or gear while in dock or storage.
Servicing a bulk hauler with loading and unloading, plus running shuttle traffic down to a planet if necessary.
Loading using exos or ground loaders in a market or spaceport.
Repair something. Could be anything from a spaceship, large vehicle or building to harvest machin- ery, a furnace or logging equipment.
Represent a group of plebeians, workers or the Free League during negotiations.
A cult stands in the PCs' way. They could be withholding relics, blocking roads or trying to stop the construction of a temple or the fulfilling of a prophecy.
The party is subjected to nature's wrath. It could be anything from ion storms, bad weather and meteorite showers to landslides or flash floods.
The end is nigh! A doomsday prophecy has been spoken that complicates the voyage.
Something important is missing. It could be gear, fuel, raw materials, and knowledge or simply birr.
For some reason, the food will not last.
A diva appears, in the form of a prophet, preacher or temple officer, hindering the group unless they are prepared to grovel.
The Icons manifest themselves somehow. Through an avatar, an omen, a miracle or some other way of the GM's choosing.
A ban or high fee complicates the voyage.
The party is subjected to nature's wrath. It could be anything from ion storms, bad weather and meteorite showers to landslides or flash floods.
A competing party has the same goal as the expedition and tries to get there first or stop the PCs. They have roughly the same gear as the PCs.
Something important is missing. It could be gear, fuel, raw materials, and knowledge or simply birr.
The group's gear is unfit for the task.
A diva appears, in the forms of an actor, director or artist, hindering the group unless they are pre- pared to grovel.
A violent event occurs, such as a war breaking out.
The employer has thugs pushing the group to work faster. It could be stevedore aqbars, foremen or something similar.
The party is subjected to nature's wrath. It could be anything from ion storms, bad weather and meteorite showers to landslides or flash floods.
Corsairs or bandits attack the group's work site.
Something important is missing. It could be gear, fuel, raw materials, and knowledge or simply birr.
For some reason, the food will not last.
A faction is blocking the work the group is supposed to do.
Rebels violently try to stop the group's work.
Bauxite (aluminum), lead glance, gold-quartz, cassiterite (tin), malachite (copper), magnetite (iron), platinum-bearing sand, sphalerite (zinc)
Pure minerals, salt
Bars of metal
Argon, helium, neon, krypton, radon, xenon
Pine, jacaranda, mahogany, oak
Water ice or rare frozen solution
Industrial chemicals
Natural (droppings) or synthetic
Fabrics (wool, velvet, silk) or clothing

Base foods such as chickpeas, soybeans and other legumes, grains (corn, barley, rice, wheat) or refined versions thereof (such as couscous) or vegetables such as aubergine, spinach, zucchini, cucumber or tomato.
Jasmine, cinnamon, cloves, cumin, mint, basil, oregano, rose water, saffron
Apricots, bananas, baklava, dates, coconut, almonds, marzipan, nuts (pecans, pistachios, walnuts), raisins, oysters, caviar, testicles, ants
Vaccines, medicines, m- and t-doses, surgical gear for bionics or cybernetics
Altars, prayer towers, dismantled chapels, icons, reliquaries, religious art, talismans, relics, scrolls
Different makes and types, for exos, vehicles, cybernetics, medical technology, prospecting gear, drones, weapons, armor, spaceships or colony life support systems
Modules, features, parts for/from dismantled ships
Exo shells, loader exos, diver exos, carrier exos etc. Stacked effective use of cargo space.
Parts or ready-to-use automatic systems
Disassembled
Choose from the Gear chapter
Choose from the Gear chapter
Basic gear for survival or for a specific environment
Alfalfa, tailored animal or livestock feed, synthetic fodder
Work animals or pets, usually alive if loaded in a primitive environment or in stasis if from ordinary or advanced environments
Ekilibri or nekatra are the most common, the former as plantation workers or pets, the latter as guards, soldiers or gladiators
Coordinates for an area or secret base.
Landing site in planet side wilderness. Usually far from cities or settlements.
A bazaar or market in a city or settlement.
Spaceport on a space station, asteroid or moon, or a landing strip near a larger settlement.
The surface of an asteroid or a smaller moon. Vacuum or dangerous atmosphere. Planet-like moons count as wilderness (above).
A small space station, anything from an oxygen oasis to a trade or service station.
A larger souk where trading partners meet. Usually in a larger city or station, sometimes seasonal.
A small colony, usually no bigger than a small, sparsely populated village. Far from other settlements.
A portal station next to a sun.
Onboard a spaceship during voyage or docking.
A small outpost, usually planet side. An outpost is commonly just a single building with a specific func- tion and only a few inhabitants see above.
The destination is placed under quarantine or an embargo.
A tolling vessel or some other customs ship approaches and demands to be allowed to board.
A customs officer demands to be bribed to allow the PCs through or will make sure their cargo gets tangled up in bureaucracy.
Corsairs or pirates attack the group's work site or ship.
Some form of breakdown occurs onboard, during either loading or unloading.
The group strays from their planned route and is lost on a planet or in space.
The PCs encounter a merchant who hinders them from selling at a profit or tricks them in some other way.
The market at the destination recently received a big shipment of goods similar to the PCs' and the prices have dropped.

rows.n: <1,000 km · Almost 0-G · Ceres and other asteroids

rows.d: Lead
Lava, melting point of gold
Iron

rows.n: Small ring, smaller than the diameter of a planet (5-10,000 km)
Massive, 10 AD wide and high. Blocks sunlight to the outer planets.
The belt is almost as black as the Dark between the Stars and difficult to maneuver through.
The belt is very bright and is always visible in the sky, even during the day.
A larger planet sits in the middle of the belt.
The belt is at an odd angle from the rest of the planets’ courses.
The belt is home to vacuum beings.
The belt’s size fluctuates over the segments, like the tide.
The belt contains many Portal Builder remains.
Roll D6 times on the table

rows.d: < -50 Celsius · All water is frozen and the atmosphere is very dry
-50 to 0 Celsius · Some water exists, ice age on land, few clouds
0 to 30 Celsius · Earth-like planet with clouds and polar ice
31 to 80 Celsius · Some water exists, small polar ice caps, cloudy
> 80 Celsius · No polar ice, very little water
Only desert and only underground water
Huge deserts, dry steppes and a few small oceans
Big oceans but mostly dry land
Oceans and some dry land
Occasional archipelagos and small islands
Only ocean
